passage:
After two months on the new team, Arohi sat at her desk with a blank sheet and asked herself whether the job had earned more time. The work was better than before. She had learnt two tools, and mornings no longer felt heavy. She decided to stay.

But she wanted the staying to mean something. She wrote it down: by the end of six months, lead one small project, learn a reporting tool, and earn an increase that matches the extra work. Then she went to Rekha, her manager, and asked for a review on the fifteenth of March to see how it was going.

At home she kept an updated CV in a folder, just in case the goals were missed. It was there if she needed it, and she hoped she wouldn't.

qa.q: On what date did Arohi ask for a review?
How did Arohi feel about the job after two months on the new team?
qa.a: Arohi felt more hopeful and engaged, since the work was better and mornings no longer felt heavy.

qa.q: What could Arohi do if Rekha said the goals were unrealistic, and why?
qa.a: Arohi could ask which goals are realistic and agree a revised set in writing, because a review works only if both sides accept the targets.

qa.q: How might Rekha see Arohi's request for a review date?
qa.a: Rekha may see a staff member who takes the job seriously and wants clear feedback, which makes it easier to plan growth for Arohi.

grounding: After a trial, the person stays for six more months with a written goal for skills and pay, a scheduled review and the exit plan kept ready.

"So, two months on the testing team," Rajni said, closing her laptop. "How was it, honestly?"
Jeevan took a breath. "Better than before. I actually learned the automation tools. But I'm still doing a lot of manual checks, and my pay hasn't moved since I joined."
"Are you telling me you're leaving?"
"No. I'm telling you I'd like to stay six more months, with it written down." He slid a page across. "By March: I write automated tests for two full modules on my own. And we discuss a pay revision at the March review."
Rajni read it twice. "That's fair. I'll put a review in both our calendars for 15 March."
"Thanks." He hesitated. "And if it doesn't happen, I'll be honest with you then."
"Meaning you'll have a plan?"
"Meaning I'll already have one." He smiled a little. "My CV's updated. It's just sitting in a folder."

qa.q: What date did Rajni set for the review?
qa.a: She set the review for 15 March.

qa.q: How does Jeevan seem to feel when he slides the page across?
qa.a: He seems nervous but determined, taking a breath before speaking and hesitating once, yet asking clearly for the written goal.

qa.q: What else could Jeevan do to make the March review go well?
qa.a: He could keep a short monthly note of the tests he writes, so the review rests on clear evidence of the goal.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Rajni as his manager?
qa.a: Rajni sees a fair, clear request instead of a sudden resignation, and knows what to support so he stays.

grounding: Shows the person choosing, after a trial, to stay six more months with a written goal for skills and pay, a scheduled review and a ready exit plan.

passage:
After the two-month trial on the new product line, I sat with my mentor Rafiq in the factory canteen and admitted it: the trial had worked, but only halfway. I liked the design meetings. I still spent most days fixing old drawings, and I hadn't had a raise.
So instead of leaving or drifting on, I wrote a plan on the back of a canteen menu. Stay six more months. By August: lead one small design from start to finish. At the August appraisal: ask for a pay review. If neither happens, I'll leave, and I'll be ready.
Rafiq read it and said, "Put it in an email to your manager, not just a menu."
I did that evening. My manager replied with a date, 20 August. I also started a folder with my CV and three companies I'd like to apply to. I'm Vaibhav, and for the first time in months I stopped counting the days.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav write the plan on?
qa.a: Vaibhav wrote it on the back of a canteen menu.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav feel after writing the plan and emailing it?
qa.a: Vaibhav felt calmer and more hopeful, no longer counting the days for the first time in months.

qa.q: What else could Vaibhav do between now and August?
qa.a: Vaibhav could check in with Rafiq every month on the design goal, so any slip is noticed early rather than at the appraisal.

qa.q: How might Rafiq see Vaibhav's plan?
qa.a: Rafiq sees a good start but wants it taken seriously, which is why Rafiq pushes for an email to the manager instead of a note on a menu.

grounding: Shows the person staying after a trial for six more months with written skill and pay goals, a set review date and an exit plan ready.
